relations.rationale: Dara/Cleo and Cleo/Yara both being on different teams is consistent but doesn't determine each other directly, though with only two teams it would imply Dara and Yara share a team.
Knowing Dara and Cleo are on different teams doesn't by itself establish anything about Dara and Yara without knowing the number of teams.
Dara and Cleo being on different teams implies there are at least two teams, supporting the claim of two teams.
Team assignments have no bearing on the group's admiration of progress.
Cool morning air and the smell of mulch are both scene-setting details but unrelated to each other.
Weather conditions have no bearing on the number of teams.
The smell of mulch drifting has no bearing on Finn checking the schedule.
The mulch smell is unrelated to Finn's note about planting seedlings before noon.
The mulch smell setting is unrelated to Vik setting up watering cans.
The mulch smell and settling into tasks supports the idea that the garden was buzzing with activity by midmorning.
Finn checking the schedule could lead to him noting the seedling deadline, supporting that claim.
Finn checking the schedule is unrelated to Vik's setup of watering cans.
Finn checking the schedule has no bearing on volunteers sharing coffee and pastries.
The need to plant before noon doesn't directly relate to a short break around ten, though it could constrain time management, they remain largely unrelated.
Finn's note about the noon deadline is unrelated to the group pausing to admire progress.
Team assignments have no bearing on when volunteers took a break.
Cleo and Yara being on different teams doesn't directly determine whether Dara and Yara are on different teams without more info.
Team assignments are unrelated to the sounds of rakes and laughter.
Cleo and Yara being on different teams implies there are at least two teams, supporting the two-team claim.
Vik's setup work in the morning is unrelated to the timing of the volunteers' break.
